observedBehaviour: A horizontal row cannot be nested inside another row's cell; the layout compiler refuses with a message naming LayerStack as the alternative. But a row inside a LayerStack layer builds and does NOT lay out horizontally either, so that route does not rescue it. addTimeline is affected because it builds a row internally - which puts it out of reach in the main column of any two-column page.

minimalReproduction.arrangement: The same two-child row in three placements: plain flow, a LayerStack layer, and a row cell. See also the timeline-nesting probe.

probeResult.error: cannot contain a nested horizontal row

workaround: Place horizontal pairs with anchors on a shape container. For a timeline rail, use an accent on the section holding the entries so its height derives from the entries rather than from a computed number.

sourceRun.note: The first render stacked every inner row vertically.

retiredNote: Lifted in 2.2.1. Re-running `row-nesting` against 2.2.1 shows horizontalInLayerStack true where 2.2.0 measured false, so a horizontal arrangement inside a row cell now composes through a layer stack. The anchor-on-a-shape-container workaround above still works and is what a project pinned to 2.2.0 needs; on 2.2.1 it is a choice rather than the only route.
